32661-rembrandt-van-rijn:
Malcolm Bell surveys Rembrandt van Rijn in three parts: the man, the painter, and the etcher. Nine chapters trace his birth and training, his years of wealth, and his later decline. A catalogue of works and a list of plates round out the volume.

Bell weighs the portraits, the biblical scenes, and the etchings, noting both Rembrandt's bold handling and his faults. The book gives a compact life and a guide to the art, from early portraits of his parents to the late work made in harder times. Bell also prints a chronological table, so readers can place each work in the painter's life.
